Czech

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

A minced oath of sakra.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsafra]

Adverb

[edit]

safra

  1. (euphemistic) darn, dang (very)
    Sára se tak safra ztrapnila, že odešla z večírku. ― Sarah got so darn embarrassed, she left the party.

Interjection

[edit]

safra

  1. (euphemistic) darn!; dang!; heck!; crap!; shoot!
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:sakra
    Safra, mám tak strašný kašel. ― Darn, I have such a bad cough.
    Co to safra bylo za hluk? ― What the heck was that noise?
    Safra! Obchod se zavřel, když jsem přišel! ― Dang it! The store got closed while I got here!

Related terms

[edit]
  • See sakra

Further reading

[edit]
  • “safra”, in Příruční slovník jazyka českého (in Czech), 1935–1957
  • “safra”, in Slovník spisovného jazyka českého (in Czech), 1960–1971, 1989

Maltese

[edit]
Root
s-f-r
8 terms

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsaf.ra/
  • Rhymes: -afra

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Arabic سَفْرَة (safra).

Noun

[edit]

safra f (plural safriet)

  1. a trip, voyage abroad, an instance of such travel

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the lemma.

Adjective

[edit]

safra f

  1. feminine singular of isfar

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Arabic سَفْرة (safra, “trip, voyage”), because itinerant workers would travel during the harvest season. Cognate with Spanish zafra (“sugar cane harvest”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsa.fɾɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsa.fɾɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsa.fɾa/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈsa.fɾɐ/

  • Rhymes: -afɾɐ
  • Hyphenation: sa‧fra

Noun

[edit]

safra f (plural safras)

  1. harvest
  2. crop

Related terms

[edit]
  • safári

Further reading

[edit]
  • “safra”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “safra”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “safra”, in Michaelis Dicionário Brasileiro da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), São Paulo: Editora Melhoramentos, 2015–2026, →ISBN
  • “safra”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Turkish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /safˈɾa/
  • Hyphenation: saf‧ra

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Ottoman Turkish صافره, from Byzantine Greek σαβούρα (saboúra).

Noun

[edit]

safra (definite accusative safrayı, plural safralar)

  1. ballast

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Ottoman Turkish صفرا (safra), from Arabic صَفْرَاء (ṣafrāʔ). Cognate with Azerbaijani səfra and Uzbek safro.

Adjective

[edit]

safra

  1. (obsolete) yellow
